findings.explanation: Every queued job failure is retried with the same flat retryDelayMs (default 15s, see DEFAULT_RETRY_DELAY_MS at webhook-queue.js:7) regardless of what the underlying error was. markFailedOrRetry (webhook-queue.js:181-185) only pulls safeErrorCode(error) for the last_error log column — it never inspects the error to pick a different delay. The Graph error classifier used upstream, core/messenger-send-errors.js, only special-cases code 10 (outside 24h window) and code 551 (recipient unavailable/blocked) as non-retryable; it has no notion of code 613 (rate limit) at all. So a 613 response takes the same generic 'throw err -> retry in 15s' path as a network blip or a 500, with no backoff — repeatedly hammering an endpoint that just told the app to slow down.

In the non-queued direct-processing path (processWebhookRequestEvents), any send error that isNonRetryableMessengerSendError doesn't recognize — which today is anything other than code 10 or 551, including 613 rate-limit — is just logged here and the loop moves on to the next event. There is no retry and no backoff for this error class in this path at all, so a rate-limited send is silently dropped instead of being retried later.
